definitions.explanation: Evoking sympathy or compassion; deserving of pity.

examples.japanese: いたわしい⟦{姿|すがた}→姿：03363_sugata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}て→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦{涙|なみだ}→涙：02235_namida⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}た→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: I cried seeing the pitiful sight.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{境遇|きょうぐう}→境遇：12097_kyouguu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧いたわしい⟦{限|かぎ}り→限り：00133_kagiri⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
いたわしい⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ニュース→ニュース：04437_nyuusu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}いた→聞く：00483_kiku⟧。
examples.english: I heard news of a tragic accident.

notes:
FORMS:
・いたわしい → いたわしく (adverbially)
・いたわしい → いたわしくない (negative)
・いたわしい → いたわしかった (past)

KANJI:
Can be written as {痛|いた}わしい or {労|いたわ}しい, but hiragana is the usual choice.

ETYMOLOGY:
From the verb ⟦いたわる→いたわる：07360_itawaru⟧ (to care for, to feel sympathy for), so the feeling is closer to tender concern than to contempt.

USAGE:
Used of a person's suffering or fate that the speaker witnesses and feels for:
・いたわしい⟦{最期|さいご}→最期：noentry⟧ (pitiful end)
・いたわしい⟦{運命|うんめい}→運命：06879_unmei⟧ (tragic fate)
・いたわしい⟦{限|かぎ}り→限り：00133_kagiri⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧ (extremely pitiful)

REGISTER:
Literary and formal. It appears in news writing, literature, and careful speech; it is not used in everyday conversation.

SIMILAR WORDS:
・⟦{哀|あわ}れ→哀れ：01775_aware⟧ - pitiful, pathetic; can carry a note of disdain that いたわしい lacks
・⟦{気|き}の{毒|どく}→気の毒：02581_kinodoku⟧ - unfortunate; the everyday word for sympathizing with someone's bad luck
・⟦かわいそう→かわいそう：02580_kawaisou⟧ - poor thing; colloquial, and used freely of children and animals
